A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same research work. Their main sections, equations, figures and appendices can be matched reliably despite additions and relocations.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original synthetic density-estimation experiments and estimates of LLM beliefs, including quantitative results in Tables 1 and F.1.

after.justification: The original empirical studies remain, supplemented by constant-tempering comparisons, marginalization validation, noise-misspecification experiments and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The core architecture, training objective and tempering/ALD pipeline remain. However, v2 specifies exact automatic-differentiation divergence for density evaluation, whereas v1 describes Hutchinson estimation (Appendix C.8 -> C.7). This changes the reported numerical procedure, although conflicting Hutchinson wording remains in v2. The joint/temp flags already existed in v1.

E1.justification: The eight synthetic targets and California housing elicitation task are retained. Appendix E.3 adds expert-response scenarios with exponential and Thurstone–Mosteller noise, alongside varying Bradley–Terry noise, on three existing 2D targets. These extend evaluation to noise misspecification without adding a new application domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the evaluated constant-tempering score–τ* comparator alongside the full-field score–τ(x) method. Previously, only the full-field method and Mikkola et al.'s flow method were compared there. The external flow comparator remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported tempering-field clipping threshold changes from the 99.9th to the 99th percentile; v2 retains 99.9% for visualization. New protocols compare joint-derived and directly generated winner marginals, vary generating noise while fixing the assumed model, and profile sampling of 25,000–40,000 points. Main sample budgets and accuracy metrics remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained joint-training illustration in Figure C.1, v2 adds substantial diagnostic evidence: constant versus varying tempering in Table 1, quantitative marginalization validation in Table C.1, noise-family/level robustness in Table E.1, and component runtime analysis in Table E.2. These directly examine several previously untested methodological assumptions and costs.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly specifies paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank testing and marks results not significantly worse than the best using underlining at p > 0.05. v1 mentioned statistical significance without identifying the test. Both versions report ten seeds and means with standard deviations; no increased repetition count is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises score-based results and adds constant-tempering results. For example, full-field Mixturegaussians10D Wasserstein changes from 1.49 ± 0.23 to 1.33 ± 0.11, and Stargaussian6D MMTV from 0.21 ± 0.04 to 0.16 ± 0.01. These accompany revised settings, so they do not establish same-setting gains. Tables C.1, E.1 and E.2 add substantial results; flow scores and Table F.1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D generalizes the one-dimensional, two-RUM reparameterization argument to a multidimensional Fechnerian-RUM derivation, explicitly addressing normalization and noise-scale invariance. The main tempering theorems remain. Appendix B also changes 'Unless p is uniform' to 'Because p is uniform,' introducing an assertion inconsistent with Assumption 3.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: score collinearity under two RUMs, a practical tempering-field estimator, and improved density estimation over flows from limited pairwise comparisons. Expanded LLM motivation and additional experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 materially qualifies the method's guarantees: Section 4.3 replaces the assertion that higher-noise mismatch is not an issue with explicit finite-noise inexactness and unresolved approximation error. It also discusses estimator bias, identifiability requiring known noise, slower sampling than flows, and uncertain pointwise density reliability. Appendix E.3 adds interpretations of robustness under misspecification.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code repository statement, discloses importance-weight clamping to the 1st–90th percentiles and the distinct 2D domain scaling, and reports component runtimes. Appendix G documents LLM assistance with implementation and checking. These supplement already detailed implementation information; newly disclosed settings do not alone establish changed experiments.

R1.justification: The introduction adds positioning against direct probability, sample and moment elicitation from LLMs, citing Capstick, Requeima, Binz and Halawi. Additional references cover prior elicitation, ratio estimators and diffusion-density limitations; Wang et al.'s Patch Diffusion citation is removed. Positioning relative to preferential normalizing flows remains central.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the introduction and tempering explanation, expands the method and LLM-experiment descriptions, and adds an appendix roadmap, notation list and reproducibility statement. Algorithms move into the main text and Appendix F.2 is relocated. The overall section sequence and narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially: Table 1 adds a third method per metric, removes its sampling-density column and changes significance markings; Tables C.1, E.1 and E.2 are new. A notation display is added and algorithm panels move into the main text. Existing figures retain their visual content, while Table F.1 is relocated beside the LLM plots.

improvement.justification: New controls, marginalization checks and robustness experiments strengthen v1's validation, while clearer finite-noise limitations and code/runtime disclosures improve transparency. These useful, targeted gains are partly offset by the new uniform-p assertion in Appendix B and inconsistent relative percentages in Table C.1, limiting the reliability of some added material.
